newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Two S.Korean bankers arrested over Hanbo scandal.
newsitem.headline: Two S.Korean bankers arrested over Hanbo scandal.

text.p: South Korean prosecutors on Wednesday arrested two leading bankers on charges of bribery in connection with huge loans extended to the troubled Hanbo Steel Co, prosecution officials said.
Sheen Kwang-shik, president of Korea First Bank, and Woo Chan-mok, head of Cho Hung Bank, were taken to a Seoul prison, they said.

The move follows the arrest on Friday of Hanbo Group founder Chung Tae-soo, who was still being grilled by prosecutors on whether he provided kickbacks to other bankers or politicians, the officials said.
Prosecutors accused Sheen and Woo of taking 400 million won ($460,000) each from Hanbo in return for huge loans from the two banks.
Prosecutors had also questioned Lee Hyung-koo, former chief of the state-run Korea Development Bank, but allowed him to return home, senior prosecutor Choi Byung-koog said.

The three banks are the main creditors of Hanbo Steel, which accumulated about five trillion won ($5.8 billion) in loans from 61 banks and financial institutions before it was declared insolvent on January 23.
